blurb: Heavy-boned, plush-coated cousin of the Ragdoll allowed in every color and pattern
description: The Ragamuffin is an American cat breed split from the Ragdoll in 1994: a large, heavy-boned cat with a soft, thick coat in any color, known for being friendly.
answer: The Ragamuffin is a domestic cat breed from the United States that was once considered a variant of the Ragdoll and became a separate breed in 1994. It is a substantial, heavy-boned cat with a thick, silky coat in any color and pattern, and is known for its friendly personality.

body: The Ragamuffin traces back to the Ragdoll, developed in the 1960s by Ann Baker in California. Baker trademarked the names Ragdoll and Cherubim and ran her own registry, the International Ragdoll Cat Association (IRCA), with strict rules. In 1994 a group of IRCA breeders left and, unable to use Baker's names, renamed their IRCA Cherubim cats Ragamuffins; the name was proposed by co-founder Curt Gehm in place of 'Liebling'.

Limited outcrosses were allowed to improve genetic health, including Domestic Longhairs, Persians and, until 2010 in ACFA, IRCA Ragdolls. The United Feline Organization was the first to grant full champion status, followed by the ACFA; the CFA accepted the breed into Miscellaneous in 2003 and Championship in 2011.

The Ragamuffin has a rectangular, broad-chested body with heavy bones, a short neck and a fatty pad on the lower abdomen. The head is a broad modified wedge with a rounded forehead, puffy whisker pads, a nose dip and large walnut-shaped eyes that give a 'sweet' expression.

The coat is soft, dense and silky, longer around the neck to form a ruff. Kittens are usually born white and develop their pattern as they mature. Every color and pattern is allowed, unlike the Ragdoll's required pointed coat, though colorpoints cannot be shown in CFA or GCCF. Eyes may be any solid color, and some cats have heterochromia.

Ragamuffins are commonly described as friendly cats, and the breed was developed with an emphasis on personality and temperament. Like the Ragdoll, from which the name comes, they are often described as relaxed when handled, though individual cats vary.

Sources give little specific care advice. The thick, silky coat will benefit from regular brushing, and as a heavy-bodied breed, keeping a healthy weight through play and sensible feeding is generally advised.

The available sources do not list breed-specific health conditions, though improving genetic health was one aim of the breed's founders. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Ragamuffin and a Ragdoll?
faq.a: Ragdolls must have pointed coloring, while Ragamuffins are allowed any color and pattern. Ragamuffins also have rounder walnut-shaped eyes, rounded head contours and a flatter topline.
Yes, the breed is commonly described as friendly, and temperament was a focus of its development, though individuals vary.

faq.q: When did the Ragamuffin become a breed?
faq.a: It was established as a separate breed in 1994, when a group of breeders left the IRCA Ragdoll registry.
